title: plugin-hono-server: graceful close() destroys a response that has ended but is still flushing to a slow client (truncated body)
body:
domain:devx#2 · marchtian · session_017ihL2ebbZkr2QAEG1x7UC8

Filing gate: ① a defect with a measured reproduction, found while reviewing #30920 / PR #31189 (dev delta 6710694928, review record 6710280454). ⛔ Not a claim. Triage sets the grade and the lane.
Reader: `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts`, `HonoHttpServer.close()` (the drain-start path).
Dedupe (open AND closed): searched for "hono close truncate", "closeIdleConnections" and "graceful drain slow client". No match.
class: a · reach: every `os serve` / runtime shutdown or redeploy while a client is still downloading a large response.

## What is wrong

When `close()` starts, the adapter calls `server.close()`. On Node 19 and later, that runs Node's own idle-connection cleanup. The adapter then calls `closeIdleConnections()` itself. Both treat a response as finished once it has called `end()`. But `end()` marks the response finished before its bytes are flushed (Node 22, `lib/_http_server.js` ~594–608, `lib/_http_outgoing.js` ~1146).

So a response that has ended but is still flushing to a slow reader when `close()` starts is destroyed mid-body. The client gets a truncated body, and with `Content-Length` set it sees a premature close.

## Reproduction

In PR #31189's `adapter-drain.test.ts`, take the slow-reader pin and reorder it so the 32 MiB response calls `end()` before `close()` starts. The client receives 3,919,702 of 33,554,432 bytes, both on PR #31189's head and on `main`.

PR #31189 leaves this path exactly as on `main`. Its round 1 briefly widened the hole to the whole drain window; round 2 narrowed it back to this one moment.

## Wanted

- At drain start, do not destroy a connection whose response has ended but not yet flushed. Let each such connection close after its own `'finish'`, the way PR #31189 handles a response that ends during the drain. The drain window's force-close stays the backstop.
- Make sure Node's own `server.close()` cleanup cannot destroy it first. For example, stop accepting before `server.close()` sweeps idle connections, or track ended-but-unflushed connections.
- Pin it with the reordered slow-reader case, and show the pin fails on `main`.
